summary: Step 7 is Track 2 (drug repurposing): given the confirmed diagnosis — the child carries two broken copies of BUB1B, one making no protein (a truncating/null allele) and one making a weakened protein (a missense/hypomorph allele) — it asks which already-approved drugs have real evidence for four mechanistic directions (D1 strengthen the checkpoint, D2 exploit the resulting aneuploid-cell stress, D3 stabilise the remaining protein, D4 treat the resulting tumour). This step is explicitly not blind: it only starts once step 6 has confirmed the pair, and every fact it draws from earlier steps was unblinded first. It graded 329 approved drugs on a five-rung evidence ladder fixed before any drug was looked up, against two decoy-gene cards run through the identical pipeline as a specificity control. Eleven drugs carry a cited, curated mechanism result (rung 2 or 3); fifty more reach the top automated rung only because they are already in a paediatric rhabdomyosarcoma trial (a fact about the tumour, not a mechanism finding attributable to this gene); a decoy gene got 64 such drugs with the gene never consulted. A do-not/caution table flags 13 spindle-poison chemotherapy drugs (including the vincristine this tumour type is normally treated with) as needing the very checkpoint that is broken — flagged for the treating team, not advice to withhold. All seven pre-registered claims were supported, and a fourth mechanism-card revision (v4, adding step 8's measured aneuploidy-burden fact) moved no rung and no table row.
why: A drug-repurposing search over a confirmed rare-disease gene is exactly the kind of result that looks meaningful by construction: any gene has trials, labels and PubMed hits attached to it, and a pipeline that reports 'N approved drugs found' without a control cannot distinguish real mechanism evidence from noise that any gene would produce. Building two decoy-gene cards through the identical, unmodified pipeline is what makes the automated stage's specificity measurable rather than assumed — and it caught a real problem: the first version of the ladder rule graded 85 drugs at the top rung purely because they had a rhabdomyosarcoma trial, a rule the decoy comparison showed was gene-independent and had to be narrowed before any verdict was drawn. Without that check, the report would have presented 85 unrelated approved drugs as if they were BUB1B-specific mechanism evidence.
verdict: H045 (direction D1, strengthening the checkpoint, yields no submittable drug and becomes a do-not table) is supported. H046 (D2 holds an approved compound with molecule-level cell evidence) is supported: chloroquine. H047 (D3 has an approved-drug route on the NAD⁺/SIRT2 axis with in-vivo BubR1 evidence) is supported only by proxy — the automated stage found nothing, and niacin/nicotinamide are in the ladder because a person curated them in by hand, flagged `curated_only`. H048 (D4 holds a non-cytotoxic approved agent at rung ≥2 with paediatric data) is supported: lovastatin. H049 (the automated stages are non-specific enough to need the decoy control) is supported: D4's automated drug set overlaps a decoy gene's at Jaccard 0.249, well above the pre-registered 0.10 specificity line. H050 (every argued drug has a paediatric evidence pointer) is supported: 290 of 329 graded drugs, and all 11 argued rows, have at least one. H061 (adding step 8's measured aneuploidy-burden fact to the mechanism card moves nothing) is supported: card v4's digests are byte-identical to v3's on every rung, shortlist row and do-not row.

inherits.what: Step 7 cannot start until step 6 confirms the pair — it is deliberately not blind, and every mechanism-card fact is sourced to a specific earlier entry: step 2/3 for the genotype and copy-number facts (F2–F4) that establish a null+hypomorph model, step 4 for the quantified damage estimate (F6) and the undetermined population phasing (F7), step 5 for the missense allele's structural context (F5), and step 6 for the confirmed, rediscovered pair itself (F9) that licenses treating this as a settled diagnosis worth building drug evidence around rather than a hypothesis.

hands_to.what: Step 7 explicitly left one row of the mechanism card open — the aneuploidy burden in this specific child's sample (fact F8) — for step 8 to measure. Step 8's measured detection limit and burden result feeds back into card v4, and the pre-registered digest test (H061) is the mechanism by which step 7 checks whether that new measurement changes any drug-evidence conclusion.

figures.name: evidence-ladder.png
figures.reads: A drug-by-direction grid: rows are drugs that reached rung 2 or higher on any direction, columns are the four mechanistic directions plus a pathway column, each cell showing the rung number (1–5) coloured by what that rung means (green = curated result at rung 4–5, yellow = curated result at rung 2–3, blue = automated-only trial/paediatric evidence, red = set aside as anti-direction or standard of care); a `*` marks proxy evidence for a same-axis compound rather than the named drug.
figures.means: Shows exactly which drugs earned their place by a cited mechanism result versus by trial registration alone: 11 drugs (yellow/green cells) carry curated evidence, while the larger blue block of ~50 drugs is 'already being tried in this tumour type', explicitly not a mechanism finding attributable to BUB1B — the visual distinction between rungs is what keeps those two claims from being conflated.

figures.name: rung-funnel.png
figures.reads: Funnel/bar chart from 329 graded approved (or curated) drugs down to the shortlist, with bars coloured green (argued, rungs 4–5, and shortlisted), yellow (rungs 2–3) and grey (rung 1, no evidence beyond being approved).
figures.means: Quantifies the step's overall yield: of 329 drugs graded, only a small fraction clear rung 2, and the 61-row shortlist is a small, evidence-gated fraction of everything approved — most drugs a naive search would surface (grey, rung 1) carry no direction-specific evidence at all.

figures.name: decoy-overlap.png
figures.reads: Bars showing the Jaccard overlap (shared approved-drug set fraction) between each real direction's automated drug list and the same pipeline's output for two decoy genes (NTRK3, XDH), with a dashed line at the pre-registered 0.10 specificity threshold.
figures.means: Direct evidence for H049: D4's overlap with the NTRK3 decoy is 0.249, well above the 0.10 line, meaning the automated tumour-trial stage returns largely the same drug set regardless of which gene is queried — this is why the automated rung alone cannot be reported as gene-specific mechanism evidence, and why the curated rung (rung 2–3) carries the actual argument.

figures.name: pediatric-evidence.png
figures.reads: One row per shortlisted drug with two dot columns: filled/empty for whether a US drug label has a section 8.4 Pediatric Use, and filled/empty for whether a registered clinical trial admits children in any indication.
figures.means: Evidence for H050: all 11 argued (curated-mechanism) drugs and 290 of 329 graded drugs overall have at least one paediatric pointer — explicitly labelled as a pointer to read, never a licence or safety guarantee, since a label section or a trial admitting children is not the same as an approval for this indication or this age group.

figures.name: mechanism-literature.png
figures.reads: Log-scale bars per shortlisted drug, two bars each: PubMed record count for 'drug AND mechanism/gene/pathway/protein' and for 'drug AND tumour context'.
figures.means: Purely descriptive context on how much has been published connecting each shortlisted drug to the mechanism or the tumour — explicitly stated to never move a rung on the evidence ladder, distinguishing this figure's role from the curated mechanism evidence that actually determines rung placement.
